acknowledgement.title: ACKNOWLEDGEMENT OF COUNTRY
acknowledgement.sovereigntyStatement: TO CONFIRM — Woven's closing sovereignty statement (checklist 2.3).
paragraphs: TO CONFIRM — needs Traditional Owner approval before launch. Woven's own website calls the host city Gimuy, the Yidinji name for Cairns, which suggests the naming to use here. Cairns sits on the Country of the Gimuy Walubara Yidinji people, with Yirrganydji Country along the coast. Confirm with local Traditional Owners and have them write or approve this wording. Do not reuse another event's Acknowledgement. See checklist section 2.
TO CONFIRM — Woven's closing sovereignty statement (checklist 2.3).

slides.heading: Where Collective Knowledge Leads To Collective Strength
paragraphs: Woven weaves global Indigenous knowledge and builds back our power for climate justice — strengthening the health of our planet while strengthening the rights of our people.

slides.heading: Beginning With The Rightful Return Of Lands
paragraphs: We envision a climate-stable future that includes, values, and upholds Indigenous peoples and Indigenous-led climate solutions, beginning with the rightful return of lands and territories.

slides.heading: A Vision Carried For Seventeen Years
paragraphs: Woven's roots trace to the Indigenous Peoples' Global Summit on Climate Change in Anchorage, Alaska, in 2009. Woven launched in 2025, and this is its first global gathering.

slides.heading: Gather, Share, Resource, Amplify
paragraphs: Our work centres on gathering Indigenous Peoples, creating and sharing global knowledges and tools, mobilising resources to directly support Indigenous-led climate action, and amplifying Indigenous-led climate movements.

slides.heading: Dreaming Into Our Future
paragraphs: Together we strengthen collective Indigenous-led climate justice strategies, promote the integration of traditional ecological knowledge into global climate solutions and policies, and foster a powerful, unified voice.
